newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian cocoa marketing rates issued minus freight.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian cocoa marketing rates issued minus freight.

text.p: The official list of marketing costs from farm to port for the 1996/97 Ivory Coast cocoa season has been issued to the trade by the Caistab marketing board, but freight rates are still up in the air, industry sources say.
Exporter calculations based on the Caistab bareme, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, give a free-on-board (FOB) value of 574 CFA for one kg of cocoa.
It is made up as follows -
-- Farmgate price 320 CFA francs (including 5 CFA for bags)
-- Transported to port, bagged, export prepared 404.35 CFA
-- With 150 CFA a kg export tax, the FOB value is 574 CFA
The bareme does not differ greatly from last season, with exporter commission and transported to port, bagged and store-to-ship charges increasing by three and nine CFA respectively.
Up-country buyer commission showed a very small decrease.

But exporters and other sources said the trade was still awaiting details of freight rates, which have not yet been finalised. It is widely believed that the Caisse wants to lower the rates, but is facing resistance from shippers.

A shipping rate dispute in 1995, when the season began at the start of October, slowed arrivals until mid-November. A sudden rush at the end of November caught forecasters by surprise and pushed the monthly total over 300,000 tonnes.

"The problem is with the CIF (cost including insurance and freight to a specified destination) side. There are rumours the Caisse wants to bring these freight rates down and that's holding things up", one Amsterdam-based trader said this week.
The 1995/96 season totalled a record 1.2 million tonnes. The 1996/97 season began late on October 24.
As a rule of thumb, arrivals of 250,000 tonnes by the end of November will confirm a main crop in excess of 900,000 tonnes and a likely total of around 1.05 million, forecasters say.
"Nobody really knows what is happening at present but we would be very, very surprised if it went up to 300,000 by the end of November like last year," one buyer said.
